newsitem.title: INDIA: Costa Rica's Naranjo woos Indian business.
newsitem.headline: Costa Rica's Naranjo woos Indian business.

text.p: Costa Rican Foreign Affairs Minister Fernando Naranjo on Wednesday urged Indian businessmen to use his country as a base to expand trade and investment ties with Central and Latin American nations.
"I am sure we will increase trade between India and countries of the region," Naranjo told a business briefing in the Indian capital.
Naranjo is the first Costa Rican foreign minister on an official visit to India.
"This shows the willingness of the Costa Rican government to see how we can stregthen the good ties that exist between the two countries," Naranjo said.

"Latin America is one of our most important areas. We all are looking forward to enlarge our commercial interests," said A.S. Kasliwal, president of Federation of Indian Chambers of Commerce and Industry (FICCI).
India trade with Costa Rica stood at $0.89 million in 1995/96 (April-March) against $2.43 million in the previous year, a FICCI statement said. It did not explain why two-way trade fell so sharply.
Costa Rica along with Panama, Nicaragua, Honduras, Guatemala, and El Salvador is a member of the Central American Common Market.
Trade will be on top the agenda when Central American leaders meet U.S. President Bill Clinton during his visit to Costa Rica in May.
Naranjo said the Central American leaders will give a proposal to Clinton on the possibility of establishing a free-trade agreement between Central America and the United States.
"It will be a very important step to give more security to the foreign investors coming to Central America," Naranjo told Reuters after the business meeting.
Naranjo earlier informed the meeting that a free trade agreement between Costa Rica and Mexico had existed for the last two years.
"We are in the process of negotiating a free trade agreement with the Caribbean states," Naranjo said.
He hoped the agreement will be finalised in two to three years.
